conceptZh: 象：大象，有長長的鼻子和大耳朵；廚師動物甩麵糰，麵糰彈來彈去一筆一筆落成字。
object: a rotund cartoon chef bear in a tall hat flinging blobs of gray dough that bounce around the frame like rubber balls, and a baby elephant who trumpets with a tiny dough trunk
morph: each ricocheting gray dough ball drops one stroke into place until the dough forms 象
creativeAngle: 廚師熊自信地甩麵糰，卻甩得到處彈，每彈中一次就落下一筆；最後灰色麵糰捏出一隻小象。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip on a solid pale peach-white backdrop. Cast: a rotund cartoon chef bear in a very tall white hat and a flour-dusted apron, who flings dough with far more confidence than accuracy, plus one baby elephant that appears at the end. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 象, drawn in saturated slate-blue strokes, ending centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with margins. 0.0-1.5s: the chef bear spins a big gray dough blob on one finger like a pizza, grins, and sends it up with a flourish; it comes down and hits the floor with a rubbery bounce. The first narrated 象 lands as the blob bounces off the floor and leaves one blue stroke hanging in the air. 1.5-3.5s: the bear flings three more blobs at once; they ricochet off the walls and the bear's tall hat, boing, boing, boing, and each hit drops one more stroke into place; the bear's hat is knocked down over his eyes and he waves his arms around trying to find the next blob. The second narrated 象 lands as the final blob bounces off his belly and clicks the last stroke in, completing 象. 3.5-5.0s: the bear lifts his hat, spots the glyph, and in surprise tosses his rolling pin into the air; it spins and lands handle-down in a bowl of flour that puffs up a soft white cloud. As the word 大象 is spoken, a round baby elephant made of gray dough with big floppy ears steps out of the flour cloud and trumpets silently through a long wiggly trunk, wobbling its ears. 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is perfectly still and fully readable for the last 3 seconds while the chef bear takes a bow, balances the rolling pin on his nose, and the baby elephant stands beside him flapping its ears, to the side of the strokes. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, clear tones, no erhua, reading exactly these syllables: 象、象、大象 (ㄒㄧㄤˋ、ㄒㄧㄤˋ、ㄉㄚˋ ㄒㄧㄤˋ). The character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only. No background music, no extra speech, no subtitles or flashing effects; stylized cartoon animals only, no real people.

conceptZh: 調皮小老鼠助跑後肚皮著地滑過光滑地板，像保齡球一樣撞倒一整排藍色積木球瓶，拉布拉多警長吹哨衝進來卻滑過頭，球瓶翻滾疊成「象」字，說到大象時一隻圓圓的大象玩偶探頭看見小老鼠，嚇得跳上小板凳。
object: a row of chunky slate-blue stroke-shaped bowling pins standing on a glossy floor
morph: the mouse's belly slide strikes the pins, they tumble, spin and land in a heap that stacks into the glyph 象
creativeAngle: 改用「老鼠對大象」的經典喜劇反差：小老鼠用保齡球式肚皮滑行撞倒球瓶疊成象字，警長衝過頭增加笑點；說到大象時，大象玩偶反而被小老鼠嚇到跳上板凳，字義與笑點合一，與前版廚師熊甩麵糰完全不同。
promptEn: An 8-second bright toy-animation clip on a solid pale butter-yellow backdrop with a glossy light floor. Cast: a tiny cheeky cartoon mouse with huge round ears and a permanent grin, an original design; a big friendly cartoon Labrador sheriff dog with a star badge and a whistle; and, at the end, one round grey toy elephant. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 象, built from saturated slate-blue pieces, finishing centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with margins. 0.0-1.5s: on the far right stands a neat row of chunky slate-blue bowling pins, each shaped like one stroke of 象. On the far left the mouse crouches like a sprinter, eyes locked on the pins, rubs its paws together and wiggles its tail. The first spoken 象 lands as it points at the pins. 1.5-3.0s: the mouse dashes and dives belly-first, but its paws spin on the slick floor and it skids in a circle, bumping one pin with its nose so it wobbles but stays up. The sheriff charges in from the left blowing his whistle to stop the fun, skids straight past the mouse and the pins, and slides clean out of frame on the right with his legs paddling. 3.0-4.5s: the mouse backs up to the left edge, takes a huge run-up with stretched cartoon legs, dives onto its belly and rockets across the floor like a bowling ball. STRIKE: every pin flies up, spins in the air, and the heap lands piece by piece in the middle of the frame, stacking into the complete glyph 象, the last pin clicking into place as the second spoken 象 lands. 4.5-5.5s: the mouse pops up beside the glyph in a one-arm strike pose. As the word 大象 is spoken, a big round grey toy elephant with floppy ears and a curly trunk peeks in from the right edge, sees the tiny mouse, and hops up onto a little stool hugging its own trunk, ears flapping, in a harmless comic fright. 5.0-8.0s: the glyph 象 stays perfectly still and fully readable for the last three seconds while, off to the sides and never touching the strokes, the mouse does a tiny victory wiggle, the elephant peeks down from the stool, and the sheriff slides back in on his belly from the right, stops with a dizzy grin and a star circling his head. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, clear tones, no erhua, reading exactly these syllables: 象、象、大象 (ㄒㄧㄤˋ、ㄒㄧㄤˋ、ㄉㄚˋ ㄒㄧㄤˋ). The character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only, no subtitles. Soft cartoon slide and bonk sounds under the voice, no music louder than the voice, no flashing effects, stylized toy and cartoon characters only, no real people.
